terms.grammar: adverb, with a verb of telling or writing (perscrībere, percurrere)
evidence: Varr. R. 2 praef. 7: breviter ac summātim percurram (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Latin summarizes with an adverb and a plain verb: summātim perscrībere, to write a summary; breviter ac summātim percurrere, to run through in brief. Cicero ends a letter summātim adhūc ad tē, that is the gist so far (Att. 15.4a.1).

evidence: Cic. de Or. 2.201: perquam breviter perstringere atque attingere (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Its first senses are to bind tight and to graze, and of words also to censure (aliquem perstringere, Cic. Planc. 33), so it is clearest with breviter: breviter perstringere.

phrases.latin: itaque subsēdī in ipsā viā, dum haec quae longiōrem dēsīderant ōrātiōnem summātim tibi perscrīberem
phrases.english: so I sat down right there on the road to write you a summary of these things, which really need a longer account
Sum it up for me: what happened?

sources: Lewis & Short: summatim · Lewis & Short: perstringo
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. summarize.
